public_rationale: The MIT paper confirms a prior 61.9% ensemble result on public validation. It does not establish the claimed omission or causal exaggeration in OpenAI's graph. The graph's exact entries and evaluation settings were not recovered reliably, so neither the halfway description nor the corrected performance gap can be verified. An intermediate score on a different test set would not settle the claim.
limitations: The identified MIT figure is an ensemble result, not simply the standalone test-time-training model.
A numerical reconstruction would assess the presentation mechanism, not prove how viewers actually changed their beliefs.

our_interpretation: The causal assertion concerns the apparent numerical performance gap created by OpenAI's December 20, 2024 graph.
The plain reading is that adding relevant omitted prior results would substantially reduce the apparent advance over the field.
Halfway is read as approximately midway, not exact equality.
The mechanism can be assessed by reconstructing the comparison; actual changes in audience beliefs would require separate evidence.
criteria.support_condition: The original graph omits the identified MIT result and other comparable results, MIT falls approximately midway between the displayed o1 and o3 results, and adding the omitted results substantially reduces the apparent gap from the prior field frontier.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The graph includes those comparators, MIT is not approximately intermediate under matching conditions, or a corrected comparison does not materially reduce the apparent advance.
